newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P affirms ratings for Sydkraft.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms ratings for Sydkraft.

text.p: U.S. credit ratings agency Standard & Poor's said on Friday it affirmed an AA- long-term rating and an A-1+ short-term rating for Swedish power company Sydkraft AB with a negative outlook.
It also affirmed a K-1 short-term rating for Sydkraft.

"The affirmation of Sydkraft's ratings...follows the announcement that Sydkraft has made a bid of 2.3 billion crowns to acquire the Swedish electricity distributor and district heat producer Orebro Energi," S&P said in a statement.
Sydkraft will resume responsibility of Orebro Energi's outstanding debt which amounts to some 600 million crowns, it said.

"The acquisition of Orebro Energi will increase Sydkraft's leverage somewhat raising adjusted debt (including market value of leasing obligations) to capital to about 55 percent from 51 percent at year-end 1995," it said.
"However, it is not expected to have a significant impact on Sydkraft's cash flow and adjusted funds from operation coverage is expected to stay at around three times," S&P said.

The negative outlook reflected commercial risks in the recently deregulated market and the political debate surrounding the phasing out of nuclear energy, which would reduce the power balance and increase the need for investments in Sweden's energy sector, S&P said.

S&P also said the single A long-term and the K-1 short-term ratings of Orebro Energi remained on credit watch where it was placed on May 9 this year but that it revised the implications to positive from negative.
